desc: Amazonian and Hesperian transition undivided unit
Hesperian and Noachian highland undivided unit
interp: Upturned, ejected, and brecciated target rocks and sediments, with local areas of impact melt. Post-impact mass-wasting and fluvial-lacustrine and eolian infill of craters common
Fine-grained eolian sediments and (or) pyroclastic air-fall deposits. Linear ridges and grooves form yardangs

Flood lavas and large lava flows, undifferentiated, sourced from regional fissure and vent systems. Highly variable ages of individual flows, although generally younger in central parts of Tharsis rise
Ice-rich Amazonian materials derived from air-fall and mass-wasting erosion and transported by mass flow and underlying, relict Noachian highland materials. Modified by thermokarst processes
Landslide and gravity-spreading deposits derived from flanks of Olympus Mons and walls of Valles Marineris
Dominantly water ice and minor lithic fines; pits may be thermokarst forms produced in part by magmatism
Water ice with minor amounts of dust intermixed and as lags; local lower sequences made up of frozen dunes with interbedded ice layers
Lava and perhaps volcaniclastic flows from Elysium Mons and unknown source northwest of Olympus Mons
Volcanic edifices composed of lava flows and possible volcaniclastic rocks. Deformed by summit collapse from magma withdrawal and gravity spreading of flanks
Basin fill of eolian, lacustrine, and (or) volcanic origin. Tectonically contracted. Sinuous ridges in Argyre Planitia interpreted as inverted fluvial landforms or eskers
Undifferentiated, friable (likely fine grained) sedimentary, volcanic, and impact rocks. Altered by weathering
Noachian impact breccias, sediments, and volcanic deposits with intervening aprons of Hesperian mass-wasted materials. Tectonically contracted
Water-ice sheets as indicated by dielectric constant, perhaps emplaced by cryovolcanism or from atmospheric precipitation. Covered by thin, periglacially deformed mantling deposit
Cryovolcanic or sedimentary or igneous volcanic, ice-rich constructs. Highly degraded by mass wasting and (or) sublimation

Roughly equal proportions of water ice and lithic fines, possibly emplaced during lowland flooding events or by eolian activity. Deeply eroded but armored by impact material; lower sequence troughed likely due to compaction
Mixture of sediments and blocks of broken up, mass-wasted, and collapsed materials
Outflow channel fluvial and debris-flow deposits from catastrophic erosion of highland rocks; islands of underlying bedrock exposed

Fine-grained eolian sediments and (or) pyroclastic air-fall deposits. Modified by fluvial dissection and eolian erosion. Linear ridges and grooves form yardangs. Tectonically contracted. Channels mostly inverted. Altered by acidic weathering in places
Volcanic edifices composed of different combinations of lava flows and pyroclastic and volcaniclastic deposits. Modified by summit collapse from magma withdrawal and fluvial dissection in places
Mainly undifferentiated, degraded volcanic materials. Heavily degraded and tectonically modified
Undifferentiated friable sedimentary, impact, and volcanic materials. Tectonically contracted in places

Volcanic edifices composed of different combinations of lava flows, pyroclastic deposits, and volcaniclastic deposits sourced from degraded shields. Domed and fractured by local intrusions. Tectonically contracted
Lacustrine and (or) sheet-flood deposits. Perhaps modified by compaction and thermokarst
Basin fill of eolian, lacustrine, and (or) volcanic origin. Modified by fluvial dissection. Tectonically contracted
Undifferentiated impact, volcanic, eolian, fluvial/lacustrine materials. Locally degraded and (or) deformed
Mass-wasting, fluvial/lacustrine, and other sedimentary materials and possibly volcanic rocks in places. Tectonically contracted
Flood lavas, undifferentiated, sourced from regional fissure and vent systems. Tectonically contracted
Undifferentiated impact, volcanic, fluvial, and basin materials. Heavily degraded; tectonically deformed in places
Primitive, degraded crustal rocks uplifted by large, basin-forming impact. Dissected by basin-related fault structures and erosional valleys
Drop moraines left by cold-based glaciers
Residual ice (H2O in northern cap and mainly CO2 in southern cap) with dust lags trapped in north polar pits. Margins and surface of unit actively changing due to ice accumulation and ablation
Wind-blown sand organized into variety of dune forms owing to variable wind activity and permafrost development
Largely unmodified flood lavas, including lava channels and other morphologies; sourced from fissures and shields
Largely unmodified lava flows and vents; vents and flows not differentiated at map scale
Ice-rich eolian, lacustrine, and (or) volcanic air-fall deposits. Margins eroded and back-wasted

Fluvial/lacustrine/marine and colluvial sediments sourced from circum-lowland outflow channels and bounding highland terrains; likely intercalated with and underlain by lava and volcaniclastic rocks. Pervasively modified and obscured by periglaciation, sedimentary diapirism, and particulate mantling
Mass-wasting, fluvial/lacustrine, and possibly other sedimentary materials and volcanic rocks in places. Tectonically contracted
Flood lavas and large lava flows, undifferentiated, sourced from regional fissure and vent systems
Volcanoes and lava flows
Undifferentiated impact, volcanic, fluvial, and basin material. Lightly to heavily degraded and (or) deformed
Degraded lava and volcaniclastic flows. Tectonically contracted
Ice-rich loess. Periglacial modification formed thumbprint terrain
Undifferentiated impact, volcanic, fluvial, and basin materials. Moderately to heavily degraded
Ancient, degraded crustal rocks uplifted by large, basin-forming impacts. Dissected by basin-related fault structures and erosional valleys
source: Tanaka, K.L., and others, 2014, Geologic map of Mars: USGS Scientific Investigations Map 3292, https://doi.org/10.3133/sim3292. Unit interpretations quoted from the map's Description of Map Units.
